title: Add structured-output validation quickstart and RAG snapshot tests
author: Noah Kim
release_notes: Adds a quickstart that demonstrates schema/structured-output validation for RAG agents, including snapshot-based regression tests and a CI smoke job.
description:
Summary: Introduces a new quickstart that demonstrates how to author RAG agents that emit structured JSON output and how to validate that output with schema checks and snapshot regression tests.

Motivation: We frequently see RAG integrations drift when prompts or index content change; teams want a low-friction way to codify expected output shape and catch regressions early in CI. This quickstart provides a minimal, runnable example that combines: 1) a small local index builder (embeddings mocked for CI), 2) a sample agent that returns structured JSON (answer + citations + metadata), 3) a lightweight validator using JSON Schema + hand-rolled assertions, and 4) a snapshot test harness that records canonical responses for representative queries.

What is included:
- quickstarts/rag-structured-output/README.md: usage guide and design notes.
- quickstarts/rag-structured-output/runner.py: small reference agent that calls Redwood API-compatible wrapper (local mode) and enforces structured output via schema.
- quickstarts/rag-structured-output/schema.json: example JSON Schema for expected agent response.
- quickstarts/rag-structured-output/snapshots/: two recorded responses for smoke queries.
- .github/workflows/rag-structured-output-smoke.yml: CI workflow that runs index build (mock), starts runner in test mode, and asserts snapshots match.
- tests/e2e/test_structured_output.py: pytest harness that validates schema and records/fails on snapshot mismatches.

How to run locally:
1) python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
2) pip install -r quickstarts/rag-structured-output/requirements.txt
3) export REDWOOD_API_KEY="<local-or-hosted-key>"
4) python quickstarts/rag-structured-output/runner.py --mode interactive "What sources support using OAuth for data connectors?"

The runner prints a structured JSON object that matches schema.json; the README includes a checklist for converting the example to your app.

Example expected output shape (human-readable excerpt): {"answer": "Yes — Redwood supports OAuth connectors via the ...", "citations": [{"id": "doc-42", "cursor": 1, "text_snippet": "..."}], "metadata": {"confidence": 0.92, "model": "mistral-7b"}}

Testing & CI:
- The CI job runs with mocked embeddings and a pinned prompt template to ensure determinism.
- Snapshot files are stored under the quickstart and compared with responses; differences fail the job to catch regressions.
- The pytest harness includes an option --update-snapshots for maintainers to intentionally refresh snapshots after intentional behavior changes.

Commits in this PR (high level):
- feat(quickstart): add structured-output quickstart scaffold and README
- feat(test): add snapshot harness and pytest assertions
- ci: add smoke workflow and mock index builder
- docs: clarify migration path for teams

Review conversation (high level):
- Sofia Morales: requested clearer instructions for offline/local mode and asked that schema.json include example values; author updated README and added examples to schema.json (resolved).
- Ari Gupta: pointed out a nondeterministic prompt token (edge case with system message) and requested a pinned-template in tests; author added pinned template and added CI seed to the workflow (resolved).
- Lena Zhou: suggested adding a short section describing failure modes and recommended guardrails for production rollouts; added a 'When things go wrong' section to README (resolved).
- CI flakiness: initial CI run failed due to a timeout in the mocked index builder; increased timeout and switched to a simpler in-memory index in CI (re-run passed).

Files changed (high level): ["quickstarts/rag-structured-output/README.md", "quickstarts/rag-structured-output/runner.py", "quickstarts/rag-structured-output/schema.json", "quickstarts/rag-structured-output/snapshots/sample_query_1.json", "quickstarts/rag-structured-output/snapshots/sample_query_2.json", "tests/e2e/test_structured_output.py", ".github/workflows/rag-structured-output-smoke.yml"]

Deployment/Merge notes:
- Non-breaking: only adds a new quickstart and CI job.
- Merged via squash after approvals from reviewers.
- Added to Quickstarts index in docs side navigation (follow-up small PR will update docs site landing page).

Known limitations & follow-ups:
- This example uses a simplified validation checker; recommend teams integrate their canonical schema registries for production.
- Snapshot storage is intentionally in-repo for the quickstart; larger projects should store golden responses in an artifact store.
- Follow-up tickets: ENG-2210 (automate snapshot promotion), ENG-2211 (add TypeScript variant for the runner).
